script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: "Breaking Point"

FADE IN:

EXT. WILLIAMS PARK - DAY

A picturesque, sprawling sports complex. Baseball diamonds dot the landscape. CHRIS JENKINS, a grizzled, 35-YEAR-OLD baseball coach, walks along the outfield fence, contemplative.

(INT. CHRIS'S OFFICE - DAY)

INT. CHRIS'S OFFICE - DAY

Chris sits at his desk, surrounded by baseball memorabilia. He stares at a faded photograph of himself, a young pitcher in a baseball uniform. His eyes fill with sadness.

(INT. LOCKER ROOM - DAY)

INT. LOCKER ROOM - DAY

Chris addresses his team. Their faces show a mix of determination and apprehension.

CHRIS
Gentlemen, we've reached the playoffs. But I've decided to retire.

A shocked silence fills the room.

MIKE
Retire? You can't retire, Coach!

JIM
But...we need you!

Chris nods, a look of understanding in his eyes.

CHRIS
I know. But it's time for me to move on.

(INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY)

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Chris meets with MELANIE, a former student and budding entrepreneur.

MELANIE
Coach Jenkins! I was thrilled when you reached out. How can I help?

CHRIS
I've decided to transition into business. I want to start a sports training facility.

Melanie smiles, her eyes alight with excitement.

MELANIE
That's fantastic! I'll help you in any way I can.

(INT. GYM - DAY)

INT. GYM - DAY

Chris trains, determined to regain his physical prowess. He sweats, strains, and pushes himself to the breaking point.

(EXT. SPORTS COMPLEX - NIGHT)

EXT. SPORTS COMPLEX - NIGHT

A heavy rain pours down, flooding the baseball fields. Chris stands alone, gazing at the complex.

CHRIS (voiceover)
It's time for a new chapter.

(INT. OFFICE - DAY)

INT. OFFICE - DAY

Chris signs the final papers for his business. He looks up, a proud smile on his face.

CHRIS
I did it.

(EXT. SPORTS COMPLEX - DAY)

EXT. SPORTS COMPLEX - DAY

The sun rises over the complex, casting a golden glow on the fields. Chris, dressed in business attire, walks proudly through the gates.

FADE OUT.

---

End of screenplay.
